text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Bulgaria's parliament approved the cabinet's privatisation programme until the end of this year. The government expects some 601 billion levs revenue from the planned sale of 583 state firms.

-- Bulgaria may reschedule for 1998 repayment on a 100,000 tonnes of wheat deal with Poland, Bulgaria's ambassador to Warsaw, Alexander Dimitrov, said. Bulgaria imported 100,000 tonnes of wheat from Poland earlier this year against exports of the same quantity from the new crop.

-- Interior Minister Bogomil Bonev said he may disband the Sofia riot police squad after 15 riot policemen were involved in a fight with civilians in central Sofia on Wednesday. Sofia police chief Emil Tanev said a few riot policemen were under investigation on corruption charges.
-- Bulgaria's police said they had arrested 28 senior officials from "strong arm" insurance firms in a move to crack down on racketeering along the southeast Black Sea coast.

-- Bulgaria's ruling Union of Democratic Forces (UDF) parliamentary group is expected to propose amendments to the constitution to expand the powers of the president, UDF deputy Ekaterina Mikhailova said.
Under the draft proposal the president would have the power to disband parliament if the biggest parliamentary group failed to form a government in one week.
-- Bulgaria's cabinet is expected to raise international road cargo transport licences for Bulgarian firms to 1.2 million levs annually from 50,000 levs.
-- Bulgaria's Privatisation Agency said it had selected KPMG Barents Group as investment consultant for the sale of two state chemical plants and one pharmaceutical producer.
-- Bulgaria's public works ministry said it had ordered two municipalities to halt the sale of land to Bulgarian-Russian joint gas firm Topenergy for the enlargement of a gas pipeline to Turkey.
-- The Bulgarian National Bank urged local commercial banks to extend loans to firms to boost industrial output, Ognyan Enchev, chairman of the Association of Commercial Banks, said.
-- Bulgaria's parliament is expected to discuss a new draft law which should protect the rights of consumers, the Fair Competition Commission said.
